# Temple Scroll Column 30 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 30 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**30:1** And you shall make an outer court: on the south side the outer court — its length one thousand six hundred cubits from corner to corner.

**30:2** From the southeastern corner going west along the south side to the southwestern corner.

**30:3** And you shall make three gates on the south side, equidistant from each other and from the corners.

**30:4** And the gates — their width shall be forty-two cubits, and their height twenty-eight cubits to the lintel.

**30:5** And each gate shall have a porch — forty-two cubits wide and twenty-eight cubits deep — and towers upon the gates.

**30:6** And on the east side the outer court — its length one thousand six hundred cubits from corner to corner.

**30:7** From the southeastern corner going north along the east side to the northeastern corner.

**30:8** And you shall make three gates on the east side, equidistant from each other and from the corners.

**30:9** And the gates shall have the same measurements: forty-two cubits wide and twenty-eight cubits high.

**30:10** And each gate shall have a porch with the same measurements, and towers upon them.

**30:11** And on the north side the outer court — its length one thousand six hundred cubits from the northeastern corner going west to the northwestern corner.

**30:12** And you shall make three gates on the north side, equidistant from each other and from the corners, with the same measurements.

**30:13** And on the west side the outer court — its length one thousand six hundred cubits from the northwestern corner going south to the southwestern corner.

**30:14** And you shall make three gates on the west side, equidistant from each other and from the corners, with the same measurements.

**30:15** And the total perimeter of the outer court shall be six thousand four hundred cubits, a square from corner to corner.

**30:16** And the wall of the outer court shall be seven cubits wide and forty-nine cubits high, built upon foundations of hewn stone to a depth of three cubits into the ground.

---

*EMET notes: Column 30 well preserved. The outer court at 1,600 cubits per side (approximately 730 meters / 2,400 feet) vastly exceeds any historical temple. Twelve gates total (3 per side) correspond to the twelve tribes. Gate proportions maintain the 3:2 ratio (42:28). The 6,400-cubit perimeter is noted explicitly. Wall height of 49 cubits (7 x 7) reflects the scroll's numerological symbolism.*
